name: manual_0c78b1
claim: When extracting or inspecting a secret from a config file via a shell one-liner, never use a bare grep/cat on the raw file -- pipe through a redaction step or use a script that only reports length/presence, even when the extraction command's PRIMARY purpose looks safe (e.g. checking a var name exists)

decisions.notes: Leaked a live secret into a conversation transcript twice in one session: once via a Python redaction helper that only checked top-level dict keys for 'key'/'token'/'secret' and missed a nested apiKey field, and again via a plain 'grep -n' on a .env.local file that printed full KEY=value lines including two real credentials. Both times the intent was innocuous (checking config shape / whether a var was set), but the mechanical command chosen printed the raw value anyway. The fix going forward: always use length-only checks (${#VAR} chars) or a script that explicitly strips values before printing, never a bare grep/cat/json.dumps on a file known or suspected to contain secrets -- regardless of how confident the redaction logic looks, because shallow (non-recursive) checks miss nested fields and grep has no concept of redaction at all.
